{{Short description|Concept in algebraic geometry}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Frobenius splitting''', introduced by [[Vikram Bhagvandas Mehta|Mehta]] and [[Annamalai Ramanathan|Ramanathan]],{{sfnp|Mehta|Ramanathan|1985}} is a splitting of the [[injective function|injective]] [[morphism]] <math>\mathcal{O}_X\to F_*\mathcal{O}_X</math> from a [[structure sheaf]] <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math> of a [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] <math>p>0</math> variety <math>X</math> to its image <math>F_*\mathcal{O}_X</math> under the [[Frobenius endomorphism]] <math>F_*</math>.

Brion and [[Shrawan Kumar (mathematician)|Kumar]] give a detailed discussion of Frobenius splittings.{{sfnp|Brion|Kumar|2005}}

A fundamental property of Frobenius-split [[projective scheme]]s <math>X</math> is that the [[higher cohomology]] <math>H^i(X,L)</math> (<math>i>0</math>) of [[ample line bundle]]s <math>L</math> vanishes.
